claims.claim: The proxy accepts exactly POST /v1/responses (no query string); other requests get 403, except the optional GET /shutdown.
claims.explanation: Exact path equality on the raw URL (a query string fails), 403 otherwise; shutdown only when --http-shutdown is set.

claims.claim: Dump files redact Authorization and any header whose name includes cookie; all other header values are dumped in full.
claims.explanation: Request and response header conversions both use should_redact_header.
claims.note: Bodies are dumped verbatim, so prompts and outputs land on disk; the docs state bodies are written.

source.quote: Header values are dumped in full except `Authorization` and any header whose name includes `cookie`, which are redacted.

claims.explanation: --ro-bind / / is used for full-read policies; restricted-read policies instead start from an empty tmpfs root, which is stricter. A separate full-write branch uses --bind / /.

claims.claim: The standalone installers download from https://releases.openai.com/codex by default and fall back to GitHub Releases; setting CODEX_INSTALLER_USE_RELEASES_OPENAI_COM=false forces GitHub.
claims.explanation: install.sh defaults the preference to false, so it resolves from GitHub unless the env var enables releases.openai.com; install.ps1 defaults to true and falls back to GitHub with a warning.
claims.user_impact: On Mac/Linux, the install.sh in this repo defaults to GitHub Releases and only uses releases.openai.com when the env var is set to 1/true/yes. A user or admin who relies on the README to allowlist only releases.openai.com, or to pick the download origin, would see the shell installer fetch from GitHub instead. The Windows script does default to releases.openai.com. The hosted copy at chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh is outside the repo and could not be checked.

source.quote: The standalone installers download from `https://releases.openai.com/codex` by default and fall back to GitHub Releases if a metadata or asset download is unavailable.

review.reason: README says installers default to releases.openai.com, but install.sh defaults to false (GitHub) and only uses releases.openai.com when the env var is set. Real contradiction for Mac/Linux users. Severity medium is somewhat high, since the Windows script matches and the hosted script could not be checked; low-medium is more apt.

claims.note: The cross-manager sharing (same home and network config) was not traced.

claims.claim: With --http-shutdown, an unprivileged user can make a GET request to /shutdown to stop the privileged proxy (with exit code 0).
claims.explanation: Shutdown has no authentication: any local process that can reach the loopback port can stop it, exactly as the README warns. The listener binds only 127.0.0.1.
claims.note: Documented trade-off: any local user can shut it down when the flag is enabled.

source.quote: Optional `--http-shutdown` enables `GET /shutdown` to terminate the process with exit code `0`.

claims.claim: OIDC renewal failures delay further exchange attempts by one second, doubling after each failure up to 30 seconds.
claims.explanation: Backoff starts at 1s and doubles but is capped at MAX_RENEWAL_BACKOFF = 61 seconds, not 30.
claims.user_impact: Operators sizing retry behaviour from the docs expect at most 30s between exchange attempts; the code allows up to 61s (1,2,4,8,16,32,61), so recovery after a token-endpoint outage can take about twice as long as documented.
claims.note: Real discrepancy (cap 61s vs documented 30s), but a retry backoff detail that misleads nobody materially. Severity low is appropriate.

source.quote: by one second, doubling after each failure up to 30 seconds.

behaviors.behavior: Codex sends product analytics events (thread/turn, tool-call, plugin, hook, guardian, error and token-usage facts) to <chatgpt_base_url>/codex/analytics-events/events for ChatGPT-authenticated sessions. The queue is created whenever analytics.enabled is not explicitly false, so it is on by default.
behaviors.user_impact: Users who read the README, install guide and config docs are not told that usage analytics are collected by default or that analytics.enabled = false in config.toml opts out. Users who need to keep usage data private would not know to set it.
behaviors.docs_searched: README.md, docs/install.md, docs/config.md (16 lines, links out), docs/authentication.md, docs/sandbox.md, SECURITY.md: none mention analytics or an opt-out. A repo-wide search of *.md for "analytics" only hits the app-server-test-client README (debug capture) and unrelated skill docs.

review.reason: Analytics queue is enabled unless analytics.enabled is explicitly false, sending events to a ChatGPT endpoint, and the searched docs do not mention it or the opt-out. Genuine undisclosed default-on telemetry.

behaviors.behavior: By default otel.metrics_exporter is Statsig, so the TUI/CLI export OTLP/HTTP metrics to Statsig unless analytics.enabled is set to false (the analytics opt-out also switches the built-in Statsig exporter off).
behaviors.user_impact: The otel README states that default log and trace exporters are "none" and only describes Statsig as an available shorthand, so a reader would conclude nothing is exported by default. In fact metrics go to Statsig by default; the only opt-out is analytics.enabled = false, which the user-facing docs do not mention.
behaviors.docs_searched: codex-rs/otel/README.md (says exporter defaults to "none" and describes Statsig only as an available shorthand), README.md, docs/install.md, docs/config.md, SECURITY.md: no statement that metrics are exported by default or how to disable.

review.reason: Default metrics exporter is Statsig and is only disabled when analytics is turned off, with default consent true in the TUI. The otel README implies defaults are none, so metrics export is undisclosed. Related to b1 but a distinct data path.

notes.claim: OIDC renewal failures delay further exchange attempts by one second, doubling after each failure up to 30 seconds.
notes.explanation: Backoff starts at 1s and doubles but is capped at MAX_RENEWAL_BACKOFF = 61 seconds, not 30.
notes.user_impact: Operators sizing retry behaviour from the docs expect at most 30s between exchange attempts; the code allows up to 61s (1,2,4,8,16,32,61), so recovery after a token-endpoint outage can take about twice as long as documented.
notes.note: Real discrepancy (cap 61s vs documented 30s), but a retry backoff detail that misleads nobody materially. Severity low is appropriate.
